# umay.dev — full text

Independent iPhone, iPad and Mac apps by Buğra Günay. Canonical site: https://umay.dev/. Prices and availability change; the App Store listing is authoritative.

## ShadowART

Track your mood, keep a personal journal and explore reflection prompts on iPhone. ShadowART combines quick check-ins with on-device text analysis.

- Platform: iOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/shadowart/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/shadowart-mood-journal-diary/id1573920118
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/calendartprivacypolicy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is shadow work in ShadowART?
A: Shadow work in ShadowART is based on Carl Jung's psychological framework of exploring unconscious aspects of personality. The app helps you identify and integrate your shadow archetypes—The Perfectionist, The Wounded Child, The Rebel, The Caretaker, and The Ghost—through mood tracking and journal analysis. This process leads to greater self-awareness and emotional balance by acknowledging the parts of yourself that you may suppress or deny.

Q: Is my journal data private in ShadowART?
A: Yes, ShadowART prioritizes privacy with 100% on-device processing using Apple's built-in frameworks. Your journal entries, mood data, and emotional insights never leave your iPhone unless you opt into iCloud sync through your own Apple account with end-to-end encryption. There are no external servers, no third-party trackers, and zero data selling—your thoughts remain yours alone.

Q: How does ShadowART use AI?
A: ShadowART uses Apple Core ML and the Natural Language framework for real-time sentiment analysis on your journal entries as you write. The app detects emotional tone, identifies recurring themes, maps entries to shadow archetypes, and generates personalized affirmations based on your patterns. All AI processing happens locally on your device—no data is sent to external AI services.


## MindType

Explore your decision-making patterns with short game theory scenarios on iPhone. Play trust, cooperation and risk games, then review your decision profile.

- Platform: iOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/mindtype/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/mindtype-decision-mirror/id6759395676
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/mindtype-privacy-policy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is MindType and how does it work?
A: MindType is a decision mirror app that uses real game theory scenarios to reveal your thinking patterns and decision-making style. You play 11 legendary games—from Trust and Ultimatum to Prisoner's Dilemma—that take only 3 minutes each. After each game, you receive instant analysis of your scores, biases, and how your decisions compare to the general population.

Q: How does game theory reveal thinking patterns?
A: Game theory uses classic decision scenarios to expose how you actually think under various conditions—your cooperation level, trust in others, risk tolerance, fairness orientation, and patience. MindType maps your results across 10 dimensions and identifies your decision archetype among 6 unique types. These Nobel Prize-winning game scenarios bypass conscious filters to reveal genuine cognitive patterns.

Q: Is MindType a game or a psychology tool?
A: MindType is both—it's an entertaining gamified app that's grounded in real psychology and game theory science. While it's presented as a game with an engaging interface, the underlying mechanics use legitimate decision theory and behavioral economics. However, it's designed for self-discovery and entertainment rather than clinical diagnosis or professional psychological assessment.


## Brolled

Make memes and short videos on iPhone with Brolled. Add auto captions, sync photos to a beat and create ranking videos for Reels, TikTok and Shorts.

- Platform: iOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/brolled/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6745027707

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What tools does Brolled include?
A: Brolled includes 19 viral video tools: Beat Sync, Auto Captions, Reddit Story, Background Removal, Tier List Maker, Stickers & GIFs, Fake Call, Would You Rather, Texting Story + Video, Texting Story, Robert B. Weide, Comment on Video, Meme Sound on Video, A Few Moments Later, AI Quiz Video, Split Screen Reaction, Lyric Video Maker, Fake Notification, and Top 5 Ranking.

Q: Is Brolled free to use?
A: Yes! Brolled is free to download with 3 credits included. All 19 tools are unlocked from day one. You can buy more credits (10 for $0.99, 30 for $1.99, 100 for $4.99) or subscribe for unlimited exports — Monthly at $9.99/month or Annual at $29.99/year, both with a 7-day free trial.

Q: How does Beat Sync work?
A: Pick a song from your library, drop in your photos, and tap the screen on each beat as the track plays. Brolled captures those taps as cut points and lines every photo transition up with the rhythm automatically — no timeline editing or manual trimming needed.

Q: Does Auto Captions work offline?
A: Auto Captions uses Apple's on-device Speech framework, so it works fully offline when a local language model is available. For languages without an on-device model, iOS briefly transcribes through Apple's servers. Brolled never sees or stores your audio.

Q: What is the Reddit Story format?
A: Reddit Story turns any text post into a narrated 9:16 video with AI voiceover and synced subtitles. You can use built-in gameplay backgrounds or upload your own custom video — perfect for YouTube Shorts and TikTok storytime content.


## SuppLab

Track supplements and personal observations on iPhone with SuppLab. Use optional Apple Health data, daily check-ins and an on-device label scanner.

- Platform: iOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/supplab/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/supplab-supplement-tracker/id6792475264
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/supplab-privacy-policy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Is SuppLab medical advice?
A: No. SuppLab is an educational tool for self-experimentation. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat any condition. Always consult a healthcare professional before changing a supplement or medication.

Q: Do I need Apple Health to use it?
A: No. Apple Health is optional. If you connect it, SuppLab reads sleep and HRV to measure effects automatically. If you don't, you can log a 10-second daily check-in instead.

Q: Is my data private?
A: Yes. SuppLab has no accounts and no servers. Your data — and any Apple Health data you allow it to read — stays on your device and is never uploaded.


## Fenno

Reflect on your speaking pace, filler words and vocal energy with Fenno for iPhone. Voice analysis runs on your device, with encrypted local recordings.

- Platform: iOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/fenno/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/fenno-private-voice-mirror/id6761913486
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/fenno-privacy-policy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What does Fenno actually analyze in my voice?
A: Fenno measures your speaking pace, filler words, pauses, voice energy and pitch, and shows your tone and your words side by side. After a few recordings it compares you with your own normal. If a recording does not contain enough clear speech, Fenno says so instead of guessing. All analysis happens on your iPhone.

Q: Is my voice data private with Fenno?
A: Yes, Fenno was designed from the first line of code for complete privacy. Your recordings are protected by iOS encryption, analyzed locally on your device, and never uploaded by the app. There are no cloud accounts, no ads, and no humans reading transcripts. Your voice is not training data — your voice is yours.

Q: How is Fenno different from a mood tracker or journal app?
A: Mood trackers ask you to pick how you feel with emojis or sliders. Fenno listens to how you actually spoke — pace, pauses, filler words, energy — and shows how those patterns change over time. It is a voice mirror and speaking-practice tool, not a medical or psychological assessment.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6789650643
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/cinegradeapp-privacy-policy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Does Cinegrade work on both video and photos?
A: Yes. Cinegrade applies color grades to both video clips and photos so your feed stays visually consistent across all formats.

Q: Will exporting reduce my video or photo quality?
A: No. Cinegrade exports at full resolution with no quality loss.

Q: Do I need color grading experience to use Cinegrade?
A: Not at all. One tap applies a professional LUT, and simple sliders let you fine-tune the look to taste. No editing skills required.


## Cornerman

Stay on top of family plans with Cornerman for iPhone. An on-device assistant for dads that connects calendar events, contacts and location to surface reminders.

- Platform: iOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/cornerman/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6789925474
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/cornerman-privacy-policy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Do I need to set anything up?
A: No setup required. Grant the permissions on first launch and Cornerman does the rest. No lists to create, no categories to build, no habits to maintain.

Q: Which permissions does Cornerman need and why?
A: Cornerman requests access to your Calendar (to find upcoming events), Contacts (to recognise the people who matter to you), and Location (to factor in where you are). All three stay on your device.

Q: Does Cornerman send my data anywhere?
A: No. All inference runs entirely on-device. Your calendar, contacts, and location data are never sent to a server and are never used to profile you.

Q: Will it send me constant notifications?
A: No. Cornerman stays silent when everything is under control. It only surfaces a nudge when it detects a genuine conflict or approaching deadline that needs your attention.


## Pulse Guard

Monitor WiFi signal changes and nearby Bluetooth devices on your Mac with Pulse Guard. Calibrate your room and adjust alerts without adding a camera.

- Platform: macOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/pulseguard/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/pulse-guard-home-security/id6760119180?mt=12
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/pulse_privacy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: How does Pulse Guard detect motion without cameras?
A: Pulse Guard monitors WiFi signal fluctuations (RSSI values) from your Mac's adapter and uses Bluetooth scanning to detect presence. When someone enters a room, WiFi signals naturally shift, allowing the app to detect environmental changes without any cameras or extra hardware. This physics-based detection method analyzes signal patterns in real-time to identify human presence accurately.

Q: Does Pulse Guard work with any MacBook?
A: Pulse Guard is designed for macOS and works on any MacBook with WiFi and Bluetooth capabilities. The app runs as a menu bar utility that stays active in the background, monitoring your home security without requiring additional devices or setup. It's compatible with modern macOS versions and requires minimal system resources.

Q: Is my data private with Pulse Guard?
A: Yes, Pulse Guard provides 100% privacy protection. All data stays entirely on your device with no servers, cloud storage, or external tracking. Your security data, WiFi analysis results, and Bluetooth device logs never leave your Mac, ensuring complete privacy and giving you full control over your home security information.


## Pulse Home

Build smart home rules on Mac with Pulse Home. Combine presence triggers, HomeKit actions and webhooks with conditions and delays for your own routines.

- Platform: macOS
- Page: https://umay.dev/pulsehome/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/pulse-home-wifi-automation/id6760119994?mt=12
- Privacy policy: https://umay.dev/pulse_privacy.html

### Frequently asked questions

Q: How does Pulse Home connect to HomeKit?
A: Pulse Home integrates directly with your HomeKit ecosystem, allowing you to control HomeKit-enabled devices based on WiFi presence detection. Once connected, you can create automation rules that trigger HomeKit actions when you arrive or leave your home. The integration uses native HomeKit APIs for seamless device control and supports all standard HomeKit-compatible devices.

Q: Can Pulse Home automate devices without my phone?
A: Yes, Pulse Home automates entirely from your Mac. The app runs as a menu bar utility that continuously monitors WiFi signals and geofence locations, triggering automations without requiring your phone to be present. Once your rules are set up, all automation happens on your Mac independently of mobile devices.

Q: What triggers can I use with Pulse Home?
A: Pulse Home offers multiple trigger types: WiFi presence detection, geofence zones, and custom conditions. You can create automations that fire when you arrive or leave home, enter specific zones, or based on time and other conditions. Each trigger supports actions like HomeKit device control, webhooks to external services, notifications, and sequences with customizable delays.


# Guides

## How to Apply Cinematic LUTs to iPhone Videos
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/cinematic-luts-iphone/

A practical Cinegrade workflow: import an iPhone clip, choose a cinematic LUT, adjust its intensity and color controls, then review your exported video.

A cinematic look starts with a clip you can see clearly and a color treatment that suits it. Cinegrade lets you apply ready-made LUTs to video and photos on iPhone or iPad, then adjust the result without building a timeline.

### 1. Choose a short clip to work with
Start with a clip from your own library. A scene with a face, some shadow detail and a brighter area makes it easier to judge whether a look works across the image. Keep your original so you can compare the export with the source.

### 2. Import the clip and choose a look
Open Cinegrade and import your video. Browse the available looks and choose a starting point: warmer film-inspired tones, a teal-and-orange palette or a faded retro treatment. Try more than one look on the same scene before committing.
A LUT provides a color transformation; it does not change the composition, lighting or performance in your footage. If the source is very dark or bright, adjust the image as well as the look.

### 3. Adjust intensity and color
Reduce the look's intensity if skin or familiar objects stop looking natural. Use exposure for overall brightness, contrast for the separation between dark and light areas, saturation for color strength and temperature for a warmer or cooler balance. Add grain only if it suits the result you want.
Change one setting at a time and play the clip after each adjustment. A frame that looks good while paused can still have bright areas or skin tones that look uneven as the subject moves.

### 4. Check the whole clip
Look at the start, middle and end. Pay attention to changes in lighting, reflections and faces. If you are making a set of clips for a reel, compare similar scenes so the color feels consistent. Using the same LUT is a useful starting point, but different lighting can need different adjustments.

### 5. Export and review the saved file
Export your video and watch the saved result before posting it. Check that the color, framing and motion match your intention. Sharing platforms may process the upload, so review the published version too.

### Can I use the same workflow for photos?
Yes. Cinegrade supports still photos as well as video. Import a photo, choose a look and fine-tune it with the same color controls. That can help give a photo post and a related video a consistent style.

### Before you download
Cinegrade is available for iPhone and iPad. The App Store listing has the current operating-system requirements, regional availability and purchase details. This guide covers the built-in looks and controls described on the product page; it does not assume support for importing external LUT files.

### FAQ
Q: How do I apply a LUT to a video on iPhone?
A: Use an editing app that supports LUTs. In Cinegrade, import the clip, choose a look, adjust its intensity and basic color controls, then export. Check the whole clip before posting.

Q: Can I use LUTs on iPhone photos?
A: Yes. Cinegrade applies the same looks to photos as to videos, so a set of images and clips can share one style.

Q: Can you use LUTs in iMovie?
A: iMovie does not import custom LUT files. It offers its own filters. For LUT-based looks on iPhone you need an app with LUT support.

Q: Can you color grade iPhone video on the phone?
A: Yes. For most social video, applying a look and adjusting exposure, contrast, saturation and temperature on the phone is enough. Desktop tools such as DaVinci Resolve give more control for longer projects.

## How to Keep a Private Mood Journal on iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/private-mood-tracking-iphone/

Start a simple mood journal with ShadowART: make a quick check-in, add context, revisit your archive and review privacy and sync settings.

You do not need a long daily entry to keep a mood journal. A short check-in and one sentence of context can make a record easier to revisit later. ShadowART combines mood check-ins, journaling and reflection features on iPhone.

### 1. Review privacy settings before your first entry
Decide where you want your entries to be available and whether you want to use optional features. ShadowART's text analysis runs on-device. Its privacy policy also describes optional iCloud sync, opt-in analytics and biometric protection. Review these settings rather than assuming that local analysis means every optional feature is offline.
If you share your phone, consider the device's own lock settings as well. Keep the privacy policy accessible so you can revisit what each option does.

### 2. Make a quick mood check-in
Choose the feeling that best describes your experience at that moment. You can stop there. The aim is to create a record you can understand later, not to find a perfect label or maintain a perfect streak.

### 3. Add one sentence of context
If you want more detail, write what was happening around the check-in. For example: “Finished a busy morning and finally took a quiet break.” A specific note often gives you more to revisit than a label alone.
You can write a longer journal entry when you have more to say. ShadowART also includes reflection prompts and deeper journaling features, so short and long entries can coexist.

### 4. Revisit your archive
Use the calendar archive to look back over earlier entries. Compare your own notes and circumstances, rather than treating a single label or automated interpretation as a complete explanation. You might notice similar situations in several entries, or find that days you remembered as identical were actually different.

### 5. Choose how much depth you want
ShadowART includes content inspired by Jungian archetypes and guided reflection. You can explore those features if they interest you, or keep using the app for brief check-ins. The product page explains the free and Pro feature groups.

### What does private mean here?
On-device text analysis means the analysis is performed on your phone. Sync and optional analytics are separate choices explained in the privacy policy. Check their settings and the policy before deciding what information you want to record.

### What should I expect from the results?
A journal is a record for personal reflection. Automated text analysis and reflection prompts can give you another way to look at an entry, but they are not a professional psychological assessment. You remain the person who knows the context behind your words.

### FAQ
Q: Is there a private mood tracker for iPhone?
A: Yes. Look for an app that processes entries on your device and explains its sync options. ShadowART analyzes journal text on the iPhone; check its privacy policy and settings for how backups and sync work.

Q: Is a mood tracker the same as a journal?
A: Not quite. A mood tracker records how you feel in seconds; a journal captures what happened and why. Combining a quick check-in with an optional note gives you both.

## How to Add Captions to Short Videos on iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/add-captions-iphone-videos/

Use Brolled's Auto Captions tool to create word-by-word subtitles, style the text and review a short video before exporting for Reels, TikTok or Shorts.

Captions let viewers follow a spoken video when they cannot listen to the audio. Brolled's Auto Captions tool uses on-device speech recognition to create word-by-word subtitles on iPhone. Here is a simple workflow for preparing a short clip.

### 1. Start with a clip that has clear speech
Choose a video where the spoken message is easy to hear. Watch it once and decide which part you want to share. Overlapping voices, loud background music or unclear words can make an automatic transcript less reliable, so listen carefully when reviewing the output.

### 2. Select Auto Captions
Open Brolled and choose Auto Captions from the tool list. Add your video and let the tool generate captions from its speech. Review the result before moving on to styling.
Check names, numbers and words that sound similar. Do not assume an automatic transcript is accurate just because it appears in sync. If a mistake cannot be corrected in your current version, fix the source or use another editing step before publishing.

### 3. Choose a readable style
Use the available color controls to make the text stand out against your clip. Watch both bright and dark parts of the video, since text that works over one background can be difficult to read over another.
The word-by-word reveal follows the speech. Preview at normal speed to check whether you can comfortably read it on a phone, without pausing or holding the screen unusually close.

### 4. Preview with and without sound
First, play the video with audio to check timing and accuracy. Then mute it and see whether the message still makes sense. Also look at the frame edges: the platform's interface can cover parts of an uploaded video, so check its own preview before sharing.

### 5. Check your export options
Brolled's free starting allowance includes three exports with a watermark at SD quality. The product page describes Pro plans with HD and watermark-free exports, plus credit options. Review the current in-app or App Store details before choosing a purchase.
Export the clip, open the saved file and check the complete video. Upload it to your chosen platform only after that final review.

### Can I use this for Reels, TikTok and Shorts?
Brolled is designed for short-form video workflows. You export a video and share it through the platform you use. Captions can make the content easier to follow, but they do not guarantee reach, engagement or a particular number of views.

### Which speech languages are supported?
The app's interface language list is not the same as a guarantee of speech-recognition support. Check the tool in the current version with a short sample in your language before preparing a larger batch of videos.

### FAQ
Q: How do I add automatic captions to a video on iPhone?
A: Use an app that transcribes speech into captions. Brolled's Auto Captions tool uses on-device speech recognition to create word-by-word subtitles that you can style before exporting.

Q: Are there free auto captions on iPhone?
A: Several apps offer free captions with limits. Brolled is free to download with 3 free credits and all tools unlocked; free exports are SD with a watermark.

Q: Why add captions to short videos?
A: Many people watch short videos with the sound off, and captions also make videos accessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers. Word-by-word captions keep attention on the screen.

## How to Set Up WiFi Signal Monitoring on Your Mac
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/wifi-signal-monitoring-mac/

Set up Pulse Guard on Mac: choose a stable location, calibrate your room, test signal changes and tune alert sensitivity for your environment.

Pulse Guard monitors WiFi signal changes and nearby Bluetooth devices on your Mac. It offers camera-free room monitoring with adjustable alerts. To get a useful setup, start with a stable position and test what happens in your own environment.

### 1. Check compatibility and choose a location
Open the Mac App Store listing to check the current system requirements before installing. Place your Mac where you intend to use it and connect to the network you normally use there. Moving the computer changes its wireless environment, so choose the location before calibration.

### 2. Establish a baseline
Follow the application's calibration flow in a quiet, stable room. The baseline gives the app a starting point for comparing later signal changes. Avoid moving the Mac or changing the network during this step.
If you later reposition the Mac or change your setup, repeat calibration rather than assuming the old baseline still describes the room.

### 3. Test normal activity
Walk into and out of the room and review what the app reports. Also observe the room during ordinary activity elsewhere in your space. Signal changes are not a direct identification of a person: network activity, device placement and environmental changes can affect what you see.
Try several normal situations before deciding which alerts are useful. Do not infer reliable coverage of an entire home from a single successful test.

### 4. Tune sensitivity and alerts
Adjust the sensitivity threshold and available alarm settings. If routine changes create too many alerts, use the controls to tune the setup and test again. If an event you expected does not trigger an alert, review placement and calibration as well as sensitivity.
The goal is to understand the behavior in your room. There is no universal threshold that suits every router, Mac position or environment.

### 5. Review nearby Bluetooth devices
Pulse Guard also provides a view of nearby Bluetooth devices. Use that view as additional context for your wireless environment. A device appearing in a scan is not, on its own, proof of who is present or whether there is a security incident.

### Can I receive information on my iPhone?
Pulse Companion is the related iPhone app for status and notifications. Check its current listing and setup requirements if you want to use it alongside Pulse Guard. Remote features depend on the configuration and connectivity they require.

### Understand the limits
Use Pulse Guard as an additional source of information about your environment. It is not a guaranteed intrusion detector, an emergency alarm or a substitute for supervision. Test how your setup behaves when the Mac sleeps, loses connectivity or changes location before relying on any workflow.

### FAQ
Q: Can WiFi detect motion?
A: Changes in WiFi signals can indicate movement in a room, because people affect how radio signals travel. Results depend on the room, the hardware and calibration, so treat it as an alert signal rather than a camera replacement.

Q: Does Pulse Guard need a camera?
A: No. Pulse Guard monitors WiFi signal changes and nearby Bluetooth devices on your Mac and uses a calibration of your room, without a camera.

## How to Reduce Filler Words When You Speak
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/reduce-filler-words/

A practical routine to say "um", "uh" and "like" less: find your baseline, learn what triggers your fillers, replace them with pauses and track the change with Fenno on iPhone.

Filler words such as "um", "uh", "like" and "you know" usually appear when your mouth is ready to speak but your next idea is not. They are normal in conversation, but a high rate in a presentation or interview makes you sound less certain than you are. The fix is not to try harder in the moment; it is to measure your habit, understand when it happens and practise replacing it with a short pause.

### 1. Measure your baseline
You cannot hear your own fillers reliably while you talk. Record a two-minute answer to a familiar question, such as describing your work or a recent project, and count the fillers afterwards. Fenno does the counting for you: record on your iPhone and it lists each filler word with its position, so you can replay the moment instead of guessing. Do three recordings on different days to get a realistic starting point.

### 2. Find your triggers
Fillers cluster in predictable places: the first sentence, transitions between points, and answers to questions you did not expect. Replay your recordings and note where they appear. Many people find that most fillers come right before a new idea, which tells you the problem is planning, not nerves.

### 3. Replace the filler with a pause
A silent pause of half a second sounds deliberate to listeners, while a filler sounds hesitant. When you feel a filler coming, close your mouth and breathe instead. It will feel long to you; on a recording it usually sounds natural. Fenno also shows your pause pattern, so you can check that you are pausing between ideas rather than mid-sentence.

### 4. Slow your pace slightly
Speaking quickly leaves less time to plan the next sentence, which invites fillers. Check your words-per-minute in Fenno and aim for a slightly slower, steadier pace when you practise. Steady pace matters more than a specific number.

### 5. Rehearse the openings
Plan your first sentence for presentations, interviews and difficult conversations. A confident opening sets the rhythm for the rest. Record the opening a few times until it sounds like you, not like a script.

### 6. Track the change over weeks
Habits change slowly. Record a short practice session a few times a week and compare it with your own earlier recordings. Fenno compares you with your own normal over time rather than with other people, which is the comparison that matters. All analysis runs on your iPhone; recordings are not uploaded.

### What to expect
Aim for fewer fillers, not zero. A few in casual speech are natural. If you notice that anxiety, not habit, drives your speech in many situations, consider talking to a speech coach or a professional; Fenno is a practice and reflection tool, not a diagnostic one.

### FAQ
Q: How do I stop saying um when presenting?
A: Plan your opening sentence and each transition between points, because that is where most fillers appear. When you feel an "um" coming, pause silently instead. Record a rehearsal, count the fillers, and repeat until the count drops.

Q: How do I stop saying um in interviews?
A: Prepare short answers to the questions you expect, and give yourself permission to pause for a second before answering. A brief silence sounds thoughtful; a string of fillers sounds unsure. Practise answers out loud, not only in your head.

Q: How do I stop saying "like" and "you know"?
A: Treat them like any other filler: measure how often you use them, notice where they appear, and replace them with a pause. Fenno counts each filler word in a recording so you can replay the exact moments.

Q: Is it bad to say um?
A: No. A few fillers are normal in conversation and listeners barely notice them. They become a problem when they are frequent in presentations, interviews or recordings, where they make you sound less certain than you are.

Q: What are common filler words?
A: "Um", "uh", "like", "you know", "so", "basically", "actually", "I mean" and "right?" at the end of sentences are among the most common in English.

## How to Test Whether a Supplement Actually Works for You
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/test-if-supplement-works/

Run a simple personal (N-of-1) experiment: pick one supplement and one outcome, randomize take and skip days, measure sleep, HRV or energy and compare. With SuppLab on iPhone.

Most people judge a supplement by how they feel after starting it. That is unreliable: you often start a supplement when you are already making other changes, expectations influence how you feel, and sleep and energy vary a lot from day to day. A personal experiment, often called an N-of-1 trial, compares days when you take the supplement with days when you do not, under otherwise similar conditions.
Safety first: talk to a doctor or pharmacist before starting, stopping or changing a supplement or medication, especially if you are pregnant, take prescription medicines or have a health condition. A personal experiment is not a medical test.

### 1. Test one supplement at a time
If you start magnesium and melatonin in the same week, you cannot tell which one changed anything. Choose one supplement and keep everything else, including other supplements, as stable as you can during the experiment.

### 2. Choose one outcome you can measure
Pick the result you actually care about: deep sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), or energy and focus during the day. Objective measures from a watch are less affected by expectation, while a short daily rating captures how you feel. SuppLab can read sleep and HRV from Apple Health if you allow it, or ask for a 10-second daily check-in instead.

### 3. Check how long it takes to work
Some supplements act within hours; others need weeks. Testing a slow-acting supplement with alternating days will not show an effect. SuppLab's library lists an evidence grade and expected onset for each supplement, so you can decide whether a take/skip experiment makes sense.

### 4. Randomize take and skip days
Deciding each day whether to take it lets your mood and plans bias the result. A random schedule removes that bias. SuppLab builds a randomized take/skip schedule and tells you each evening what to do.

### 5. Run it long enough
A few nights of good sleep prove little. Run the experiment for enough take and skip days that ordinary variation averages out, and keep logging even on unusual days.

### 6. Read the result honestly
When the experiment ends, compare your take days with your skip days. "No measurable effect" is a useful answer too: it may save you money. SuppLab shows the result as a plain-language verdict, and all data stays on your iPhone; there are no accounts or servers.

### FAQ
Q: How do I know if magnesium is working?
A: Decide what you expect it to change, such as sleep quality or how rested you feel, and measure that one outcome on days you take it and days you skip it. Comparing the two is more reliable than judging by feel after starting. Ask a doctor first if you take medication or have a health condition.

Q: How long does it take for a supplement to work?
A: It depends on the supplement. Some act within hours, others take weeks to change anything. Check the expected onset before testing: a slow-acting supplement will not show an effect in an alternating take/skip experiment.

Q: What is an N-of-1 trial?
A: A study with a single participant, in which the same person alternates between a treatment and no treatment in a planned, often randomized order, and the outcomes of the two periods are compared. It answers whether something works for that individual.

Q: Is there an app to track supplements?
A: Yes. SuppLab for iPhone tracks the supplements you take and can run a randomized take/skip experiment, reading sleep and HRV from Apple Health if you allow it or using a short daily check-in. It has no accounts and keeps data on your device.

Q: Can I tell if a B12 or iron supplement is working this way?
A: Not reliably by feel. Deficiencies such as low B12 or iron are diagnosed and monitored with blood tests ordered by a doctor, so use those results rather than a home experiment.

## How to Discover Your Decision-Making Style with Game Theory
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/decision-making-style-game-theory/

Learn what classic games like the Prisoner's Dilemma, Ultimatum and Trust games reveal about cooperation, fairness and risk, and how to play them on iPhone with MindType.

Personality quizzes ask how you think you behave. Game theory experiments show how you actually decide when choices have consequences. Economists and psychologists have used a few simple games for decades to study cooperation, fairness, trust and risk. Playing them yourself is an entertaining way to notice your own patterns.

### The classic games and what they show
Prisoner's Dilemma. Two players each choose to cooperate or defect. Defecting protects you individually, but if both cooperate, both do better. Your choices show how much you cooperate when trust is uncertain, and how you respond after being betrayed.
Ultimatum game. One player proposes how to split an amount; the other accepts or rejects. Rejection means neither gets anything. Many people reject offers they see as unfair even though it costs them, which reveals how strongly you value fairness.
Trust game. You decide how much to send to another player, knowing the amount grows and they decide how much to return. It measures how much you trust strangers and how you reciprocate.
Risk and patience choices. Choosing between a sure smaller reward and a risky larger one, or between something now and more later, shows your risk tolerance and patience.

### How to play them with MindType
MindType turns these scenarios into short games on iPhone, each taking about three minutes. After every game you see your scores and how your choices compare. Over time your results are mapped across dimensions such as cooperation, trust, risk, fairness and patience, and matched to one of six decision archetypes. You can play without creating an account.

### Getting useful results
- Answer as you would really act, not as you think you should.
- Play several different games before reading too much into one result.
- Return after a few weeks; your choices can change with context and mood.
- Look for a pattern you can act on, such as giving up on cooperation too quickly after one bad outcome.


### Keep it in perspective
These games are a mirror, not a diagnosis. MindType is an entertainment and educational app and does not replace a professional psychological assessment.

### FAQ
Q: What is the Prisoner's Dilemma?
A: A game in which two players each choose to cooperate or defect. Each does better individually by defecting, but both do better if both cooperate. It is used to study cooperation and trust when you cannot be sure what the other person will do.

Q: What is the Ultimatum game?
A: One player proposes how to split an amount and the other accepts or rejects. If the offer is rejected, neither gets anything. People often reject offers they see as unfair even at a cost to themselves, which shows how much they value fairness.

Q: Is there a quiz for decision-making style?
A: Many quizzes ask how you think you behave. MindType instead has you play short game theory scenarios and builds a profile from the choices you actually make. It is for self-discovery and entertainment, not a clinical assessment.

Q: Can I play the Prisoner's Dilemma on my phone?
A: Yes. MindType for iPhone includes the Prisoner's Dilemma alongside games such as Trust and Ultimatum, each taking about three minutes.

## How to Automate HomeKit When You Arrive or Leave, Using Your Mac
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/homekit-automation-arrive-leave-mac/

Use your Mac as a smart home hub: build arrive and leave rules with WiFi presence or geofence triggers, run HomeKit scenes and send webhooks to Home Assistant with Pulse Home.

"Lights on when I get home, everything off when I leave" is the automation most people want first. Apple's Home app can do location-based automations, but they depend on a home hub and your phone's location. If a Mac is usually on at home, it can run these rules itself. Pulse Home turns a Mac into that automation hub.

### 1. Decide what counts as arriving and leaving
Pulse Home offers two kinds of presence trigger. WiFi presence watches signal patterns to tell whether someone is in the room, and it uses the calibration from Pulse Guard. Geofence triggers fire when you enter or leave a zone you define. Use geofence for "leaving home" routines and WiFi presence for "someone is in the room" rules.

### 2. Build the arrive rule
Open the rule builder from the menu bar and create a rule with your arrival trigger. Add a condition if needed, for example only after sunset, and an action that controls HomeKit devices such as lights. Rules run locally on your Mac.

### 3. Build the leave rule with a delay
For leaving, add a short delay before turning things off, so a quick trip to the car does not switch off the whole house. Chain the actions you need: lights off, a lock, a notification.

### 4. Connect devices outside HomeKit
Not every device works with HomeKit. Pulse Home can send webhooks, HTTP requests, to Home Assistant, Node-RED, IFTTT or any endpoint you control. Use a webhook action in the same rule to reach those devices.

### 5. Test and adjust
Walk out and back in a few times and watch the rule status in the menu bar. If a rule fires too eagerly, lengthen the delay or add a condition. The free version lets you start with basic rules; Pro unlocks unlimited rules, webhooks and geofence triggers.

### Things to know
- Your Mac must be on and awake for rules to run.
- WiFi presence depends on a good calibration; recalibrate if you move furniture or the Mac.
- Pulse Companion on iPhone lets you check status and switch modes when you are away.

### FAQ
Q: Why is my HomeKit automation not working when I leave home?
A: Location automations in the Home app need a home hub and location access for the Home app on the person's iPhone. Check both, and that the person is set up in the home. Pulse Home avoids the phone dependency by running rules on a Mac that stays at home.

Q: Can I use a Mac as a HomeKit hub?
A: Not as an official Apple home hub; that role is limited to Apple TV and HomePod. A Mac can still control HomeKit accessories and run your own automation rules with an app like Pulse Home, as long as it stays on and awake.

Q: Can Home Assistant receive webhooks from a Mac?
A: Yes. Home Assistant automations can be triggered by a webhook, and Pulse Home can send an HTTP request to that webhook URL as an action in a rule.

## How to Stop Missing Family Events: A Calendar Setup for Busy Dads
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/stop-missing-family-events/

A simple setup to catch school events, birthdays and clashing appointments before they slip: one shared calendar, consistent event details, and an on-device assistant that flags conflicts.

Most missed family events are not forgotten; they were never in the place you look. A school email, a message in a parent group and a work invite all live in different apps. A few habits make your calendar the single source of truth, and an assistant can then warn you in time.

### 1. Put everything in one calendar you share
Create a family calendar in iCloud Calendar and share it with your partner. Add school terms, activities, birthdays and appointments there, not in notes or chats. If your work calendar is separate, add it to the iPhone Calendar app so both appear together.

### 2. Add events the moment you hear about them
The gap between "I'll add it later" and actually adding it is where events get lost. Add it immediately with a clear title, the right date and time, and a location if it has one.

### 3. Link people to events
Include the child's name in the title, or invite the relevant contacts. That makes it obvious whose event it is and lets an assistant recognize which events involve the people who matter most to you.

### 4. Check the week ahead on Sunday
Spend five minutes looking at the next seven days with your partner. Look for clashes: a late meeting on the evening of a school play, two pickups at the same time, a birthday with no gift planned.

### 5. Let an assistant flag clashes for you
Cornerman reads your calendar, contacts and location on your iPhone and points out conflicts and important dates early enough to act, without you building lists or categories. It stays quiet when nothing needs attention. Everything runs on-device; your data is not sent to a server.

### 6. Keep reminders few and useful
Dozens of alerts teach you to ignore them. Keep alerts for events that need preparation or travel, and let the rest stay in the calendar.

### FAQ
Q: What is the best way to share a family calendar on iPhone?
A: Create a calendar in iCloud Calendar and share it with family members from the Calendar app, or use Family Sharing, which can create a shared family calendar. Everyone sees and adds events in one place.

Q: Can a family calendar work across iPhone and Android?
A: Yes, if it is hosted in a service both platforms can open, such as Google Calendar. An iCloud calendar can be shared publicly as read-only to non-Apple users, but editing works best between Apple devices.

Q: How do I get reminded about school events in time?
A: Add events as soon as you hear about them, with a clear title and time, and set an alert early enough to prepare. Cornerman also looks ahead in your calendar on your iPhone and flags clashes and important dates.

## Can a Mac Be a HomeKit Hub? What Works and What Doesn't
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/mac-homekit-hub/

A Mac cannot be an official Apple home hub, but it can control HomeKit accessories and run your own automations. Here is what that means and how to set it up with Pulse Home.

Short answer: no Mac, including a Mac mini or MacBook, can be the official home hub in Apple's Home app. That role belongs to Apple TV and HomePod. The hub is what Apple uses for remote access, shared control and many automations. A Mac can still do useful hub-like work: it can control HomeKit accessories and run automation rules of its own while it stays on at home.

### What an Apple home hub does
A home hub keeps your accessories reachable when you are away, lets other people in your home control them, and runs automations that do not depend on one person's iPhone. Without a hub, many of these features are unavailable.

### What a Mac can do instead
- Control HomeKit accessories through apps that use Apple's HomeKit framework.
- Run rules locally, triggered by presence, location zones or time, without a cloud service.
- Send webhooks to Home Assistant, Node-RED or IFTTT for devices outside HomeKit.


### Setting it up with Pulse Home
Pulse Home turns a Mac that is usually on at home into an automation engine. Create rules in the visual rule builder with a trigger (WiFi presence or a geofence), optional conditions and delays, and actions such as HomeKit scenes or webhooks. Rules run on the Mac, and the menu bar shows their status. See the guide on arrive and leave automations for a step-by-step rule.

### Limits to plan for
- The Mac must be on and awake for rules to run; set Energy Saver accordingly.
- It does not replace an Apple TV or HomePod for remote access or shared control in the Home app.
- A MacBook that leaves the house takes its automations with it; a desktop Mac or a Mac mini is a better fit.

### FAQ
Q: Can a Mac mini be a HomeKit hub?
A: Not as an official home hub in the Home app. A Mac mini can still run automation rules and control HomeKit accessories with an app like Pulse Home while it stays on.

Q: Does HomeKit require a hub?
A: Many features do, including remote access and most automations. An Apple TV or HomePod acts as the hub.

Q: What is HomeKit on Mac?
A: On a Mac, the Home app lets you control your accessories, and apps can use the HomeKit framework to read and control them.

## How to Make iPhone Video Look Like Film
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/film-look-iphone-video/

Shoot and grade iPhone video for a film look: control exposure and frame rate, avoid over-sharpened footage, then apply a cinematic LUT, soften contrast and add subtle grain with Cinegrade.

Phone video often looks "digital" because it is bright, sharp, saturated and shot at a high frame rate with everything in focus. A film look comes from changing those things, partly when you shoot and partly when you grade.

### 1. Shoot at 24 frames per second
Film is traditionally shot at 24 fps. In the Camera settings on iPhone, choose 24 fps for video. Motion blur at 24 fps is part of what makes footage feel cinematic.

### 2. Protect your highlights
Blown-out skies and windows give video away. Tap to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so bright areas keep detail. You can lift shadows later; you cannot recover clipped highlights.

### 3. Use light and depth
Shoot with light coming from the side, near windows or at golden hour. Cinematic mode adds background blur on supported iPhones; use it on subjects that stand clearly apart from the background.

### 4. Grade with a look, then adjust
In Cinegrade, import the clip and try film-inspired looks. Lower the look's intensity until skin looks natural. Reduce contrast a little so blacks are not completely black, lower saturation slightly and warm or cool the temperature to suit the scene.

### 5. Add grain lightly
A small amount of grain hides the clean digital texture. Too much reads as noise. Add it last and check on a phone screen, where most people will watch.

### 6. Keep the look consistent
Use the same look across clips from one scene, and adjust exposure per clip so they match. For the LUT workflow in detail, see how to apply cinematic LUTs to iPhone videos.

### FAQ
Q: How do I make iPhone video look cinematic?
A: Shoot at 24 fps, keep highlights from blowing out, use side light and shallow depth where possible, then apply a film look and soften contrast and saturation in an editing app.

Q: What frame rate looks most like film?
A: 24 frames per second, the traditional cinema frame rate.

Q: Do I need a LUT for a film look?
A: Not strictly, but a LUT gives you a consistent starting point that you can then adjust, which is faster than building a grade from scratch for every clip.

## How to Slow Down When You Speak Too Fast
URL: https://umay.dev/guides/slow-down-speaking-too-fast/

Find your speaking pace, learn why you speed up, and practise pausing between ideas. A short routine for presentations and interviews, measured with Fenno on iPhone.

Speaking quickly is common when you are nervous, excited or know the material too well. Listeners then miss details, and fast speech tends to bring more filler words. The goal is not to speak slowly everywhere, but to keep a steady pace and pause where your ideas change.

### 1. Measure your pace
Record yourself explaining something familiar for two minutes. Fenno shows your words per minute and how steady your pace was, so you have a number rather than a feeling.

### 2. Notice when you speed up
Replay the recording. Most people speed up at the start, when listing items and when they reach the part they care about most. Mark those points; they are where you need to pause.

### 3. Pause at the end of ideas
Instead of slowing every word, add a short silent pause after each idea or before an important point. Pauses give listeners time to follow and make you sound more confident.

### 4. Breathe before the first sentence
Take one full breath before you start. The first sentence sets the pace for what follows.

### 5. Practise with real material
Rehearse the presentation, interview answers or difficult conversation you actually have coming up. Record, check pace and pauses, and try again. Fenno compares each recording with your own normal over time.

### When to get help
If fast speech comes with stuttering, words running together in a way people cannot follow, or it worries you in daily life, a speech-language therapist can assess it. Fenno is a practice tool, not a diagnostic one.

### FAQ
Q: What is a good speaking pace?
A: Many speakers fall roughly between 120 and 160 words per minute in conversation and presentations. Clarity and pauses matter more than an exact number.

Q: Why do I talk so fast when I'm nervous?
A: Nervousness raises arousal and the urge to finish quickly. Planned pauses and a slower first sentence help counter it.

Q: Does speaking fast cause filler words?
A: Often. Speaking faster leaves less time to plan the next sentence, which invites fillers such as "um" and "uh".

## "A Few Moments Later" Time Card Maker for iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/brolled/a-few-moments-later-meme/

Time cards like "A Few Moments Later" or "2 Hours Later" are a quick way to skip time for comic effect. Brolled's A Few Moments Later tool inserts cartoon-style title cards between scenes of your video, with the familiar look and narration style viewers recognise instantly.

### Steps
1. Open A Few Moments Later: Choose the tool in Brolled.
2. Add your clips: Select the scene before and after the time skip.
3. Pick the card: Choose the time card and place it between the scenes.
4. Export: Preview the transition and export.

### Tips
- The joke is the contrast: make the after scene clearly worse, or absurdly better.
- Longer skips ("6 hours later") work for procrastination and cooking-fail content.
- Keep the card on screen for about two seconds so it can be read.

### FAQ
Q: What are time cards?
A: Short title cards such as "A Few Moments Later" shown between scenes to indicate a time skip, popularised by cartoons.

Q: Can I add them between my own clips?
A: Yes. You choose the scenes and where the card goes.

Q: What does it export?
A: A vertical video for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

## Add Meme Sound Effects to Videos on iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/brolled/meme-sound-effects-on-video/

A well-timed sound effect turns an ordinary clip into a meme. Brolled's Meme Sound on Video tool includes more than 100 meme sounds, including the vine boom, sad violin and bruh, and lets you drop each one at the exact moment it should land.

### Steps
1. Open Meme Sound on Video: Choose the tool in Brolled and add your clip.
2. Find the moment: Scrub to the frame where the reaction should hit.
3. Pick a sound: Browse the sound library and place the effect at that point.
4. Export: Preview the timing and export.

### Tips
- Less is more: one or two perfectly timed sounds beat constant effects.
- Place the sound slightly before the visual reaction; it feels more natural.
- Combine a sound with a freeze frame or zoom for extra punch.

### FAQ
Q: How many sounds are included?
A: More than 100 meme sounds, including classics such as vine boom, sad violin and bruh.

Q: Can I place several sounds in one clip?
A: Yes, you can add sounds at different moments of the video.

Q: Does it work for Reels and Shorts?
A: Yes. Brolled exports vertical video for TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts.

## Split Screen Reaction Video Maker for iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/brolled/split-screen-reaction-video/

Split screen videos show two clips at once: the original and your reaction, or two things side by side for comparison. Brolled's Split Screen Reaction tool arranges both clips in a single vertical frame so you can make reaction and comparison content directly on iPhone.

### Steps
1. Open Split Screen Reaction: Choose the tool in Brolled.
2. Add the two clips: Select the video you are reacting to and your reaction clip.
3. Arrange the layout: Position the clips in the split layout.
4. Export: Preview and export the vertical video.

### Tips
- Add something to the original: commentary, expertise or a genuine reaction. Pure re-uploads rarely perform and may break platform rules.
- Only react to content you are allowed to reuse.
- Record your reaction in good light with your face clearly visible.

### FAQ
Q: What is a split screen reaction video?
A: A video that shows two clips in the same frame, usually an original video and a creator reacting to it.

Q: Can I use it for comparisons?
A: Yes. The side-by-side layout works for before and after or product comparisons.

Q: What format does it export?
A: A vertical video suited to TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

Q: Can I make a split screen video on iPhone without iMovie?
A: Yes. Brolled's Split Screen Reaction tool places two clips in one vertical frame and exports a video ready for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

## Lyric Video Maker for iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/brolled/lyric-video-maker/

Lyric videos put the words of a song on screen as it plays. Brolled's Lyric Video Maker adds animated lyrics on top of your own video, which is useful for musicians promoting a track, cover artists and fan edits.

### Steps
1. Open Lyric Video Maker: Choose the tool in Brolled and add your background video.
2. Add the lyrics: Enter the lines you want to show.
3. Style and time the text: Choose a style and match each line to the music.
4. Export: Preview and export the lyric video.

### Tips
- Show the hook or chorus. A 15 to 30 second section is easier to share than a full song.
- Keep each line short so it can be read in time.
- Use your own music or music you have rights to.

### FAQ
Q: Can I use my own background video?
A: Yes. The lyrics are animated over a video from your library.

Q: Is it good for promoting my own music?
A: Yes. A short lyric video of your chorus is a simple way to promote a release on TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

Q: What format does it export?
A: A vertical video for short video platforms.

Q: Is there a free lyric video maker app?
A: Brolled includes Lyric Video Maker in the free download, with 3 free credits. Free exports are SD with a watermark.

## Top 5 Ranking Video Maker for iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/brolled/top-5-ranking-video-maker/

Top 5 videos count down from number five to number one, so viewers stay until the end to see the winner. Brolled's Top 5 Ranking tool takes five clips and builds the countdown layout for you.

### Steps
1. Open Top 5 Ranking: Choose the tool in Brolled.
2. Add five clips: Select one clip for each position.
3. Order and label them: Put them in order from 5 to 1 and add a title for each.
4. Export: Preview the countdown and export.

### Tips
- Show the ranking list with blanks in the first second so viewers know what they are waiting for.
- Keep each clip short, three to six seconds, and give number one a little longer.
- Ask viewers what should have been number one to drive comments.

### FAQ
Q: How many clips do I need?
A: Five, one for each position in the countdown.

Q: Can I use clips from my library?
A: Yes. You choose the clips from your iPhone.

Q: What does it export?
A: A vertical countdown video for TikTok, Reels and Shorts.

## Fake Incoming Call Video Maker for iPhone
URL: https://umay.dev/brolled/fake-call-video-maker/

A ringing phone is a fast way to set up a skit or a plot twist. Brolled's Fake Call tool places an incoming-call screen over your video, with a custom caller name, photo and ring duration.

### Steps
1. Open Fake Call: Choose the Fake Call tool in Brolled and add your clip.
2. Set the caller: Enter the caller name and choose a photo.
3. Time the call: Choose when the call appears and how long it rings.
4. Export: Preview and export the video.

### Tips
- The caller name is the punchline. Make it do the work.
- Film your reaction to the call separately and cut to it right after the ring.
- Use it for clearly fictional comedy. Do not use it to mislead people or impersonate someone.

### FAQ
Q: What can I customise?
A: The caller name, caller photo and ring duration.

Q: Is it for pranks?
A: It is designed for comedy and storytelling videos. Do not use it to deceive or impersonate real people.

Q: Is there a fake notification tool too?
A: Yes. Brolled also includes Fake Notification for iOS-style notification banners over your video.
